title: Friedgut Junta Theorem for Product Spaces
statement: There is a universal constant $C>0$ such that the following holds. Let $P$ be a finite product of probability spaces with strictly positive coordinate weights, let $n\in\mathbb N$, and suppose every coordinate atom has weight at least $\lambda$, where $0<\lambda\le 1/2$. For every function $f$ taking values in $\{-1,1\}$ and every $0<\varepsilon\le1$, there are a coordinate set $J\subseteq[n]$ and a function $g$ taking values in $\{-1,1\}$ that depends only on $J$, such that $|J|\le(1/\lambda)^{C I(f)/\varepsilon}$ and $\Pr_P(f\ne g)\le\varepsilon$, where $I(f)$ is the total influence of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a constant $C>0$ independent of the parameters and product space
Natural number $n$ and finite product probability space $P$
Every coordinate atom has weight at least $\lambda$
replaced: There is an absolute $C>0$ such that for every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, with every coordinate atom at least $0<\lambda\le1/2$, every $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, and every $0<\varepsilon\le1$, there exist $J\subseteq[n]$ and $g:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on $J$ with $|J|\le(1/\lambda)^{CI(f)/\varepsilon}$ and $\Pr_P(f\ne g)\le\varepsilon$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $I_i(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)^2$; $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|\mathbb E_Ph_S^2$; $\Pr_P(A)=\mathbb E_P\mathbf1_A$, where $\mathbf1_A$ is $1$ on $A$ and $0$ elsewhere.
